items.passage: The idea that a tool used to make you more productive at work — work that ultimately benefits the organization — is part of your pay is corporate propaganda. Pure and simple. I know someone reading this is thinking: if I'm allocated more tokens, I could be more productive and ultimately get paid better. That logic only holds if you and your employer have truly aligned incentives.

source_piece.title: Please Don't Let Your Employer Trick You Into Taking AI Tokens as Pay

hook.headline: Employees are becoming bot bosses without promotions or raises

platform_cuts.linkedin:
AI is turning workers into managers of bots — without the promotion or the raise.

The idea that a tool used to make you more productive at work — work that ultimately benefits the organization — is part of your pay is corporate propaganda. Pure and simple.

If managing agents gives you more responsibility, more output, and more accountability, companies will try to count the tool as part of your compensation. Don't let them. The productivity only strengthens the case that your work is worth more.
platform_cuts.substack_notes:

A tool used to make you more productive at work is not part of your pay. If managing agents gives you more responsibility, output, and accountability, the case is that your work is worth more — not that the tool counts as compensation.

items.passage: Step three is ownership, and this is where most companies are flying blind. The organizations figuring this out have an AI lead who is AI-native, or close to it, overseeing usage across the company. When AI lives inside the legacy IT department, you get process and compliance. Experimentation and cost discipline come from giving it its own home.

items.passage: They’ve been told AI will transform everything. But they don’t know how. So they’re waiting. They’re not hiring because they don’t know what they need. They’re unsure whether to invest in new headcount or hold off while they figure out if AI can replace those roles, where their operations are most exposed to disruption, or whether upskilling their existing teams might be the smarter bet.

source_piece.title: Why No One Can Get a Job in 2025

platform_cuts.linkedin: Companies have been told AI will transform everything. But they don’t know how. So they’re waiting. They’re not hiring because they don’t know what they need. They’re unsure whether to invest in new headcount, hold off while they see if AI can replace roles, or upskill the teams they already have. The effect on labor may show up first in jobs that never open, not jobs that disappear.
